question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- \sin{\left(2 u + v \right)} \\ \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ - \frac{\pi}{6}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- \sin{\left(2 u + v \right)}$ and $y=\cos{\left(u - v \right)}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- 2 \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)}, & x_v&=- \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)}, \\ y_u&=- \sin{\left(u - v \right)}, & y_v&=\sin{\left(u - v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- 2 \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)} & - \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)} \\ - \sin{\left(u - v \right)} & \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- 2 \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)}\right)\left(\sin{\left(u - v \right)}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \cos{\left(2 u + v \right)}\right)\left(- \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(0,- \frac{\pi}{6})&=\begin{vmatrix}- \sqrt{3} & - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ - \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- \sqrt{3}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right) \\ &=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) \\ &=- \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- \left(- u - 2 v\right)^{2} \\ \left(2 u + v\right)^{2}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- \left(- u - 2 v\right)^{2}$ and $y=\left(2 u + v\right)^{2}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- 2 u - 4 v, & x_v&=- 4 u - 8 v, \\ y_u&=8 u + 4 v, & y_v&=4 u + 2 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- 2 u - 4 v & - 4 u - 8 v \\ 8 u + 4 v & 4 u + 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- 2 u - 4 v\right)\left(4 u + 2 v\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- 4 u - 8 v\right)\left(8 u + 4 v\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(0,-2)&=\begin{vmatrix}8 & 16 \\ -8 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(8\right)\left(-4\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(16\right)\left(-8\right) \\ &=-32-\left(-128\right) \\ &=96.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- \left(u + v\right)^{3} \\ - \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- \left(u + v\right)^{3}$ and $y=- \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{3}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2}, & x_v&=- 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2}, \\ y_u&=3 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2}, & y_v&=- 6 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2} & - 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2} \\ 3 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2} & - 6 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\left(- 6 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- 3 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\left(3 \left(- u + 2 v\right)^{2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(1,2)&=\begin{vmatrix}-27 & -27 \\ 27 & -54\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(-27\right)\left(-54\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-27\right)\left(27\right) \\ &=1458-\left(-729\right) \\ &=2187.\end{aligned}
$$
